title: Teaching AI Literacy: A Foundations Workshop
subtitle: A half-day professional development module for K–12 educators
subject: Professional Development
Computer Science
Cross-Curricular
summary: Designed for educators with no prior AI background. Participants leave with a working mental model of how AI systems work, a framework for evaluating AI literacy resources, and a draft plan for integrating one new AI literacy topic into an existing course.

body.text: This professional development module meets educators where they are — curious but uncertain — and builds both conceptual understanding and pedagogical confidence. By the end of the session, participants will have taught one short AI concept to a peer and received structured feedback.

items: Welcome and framing (15 min): Why AI literacy, why now, and what it is not.
How AI systems work — an honest overview (45 min): Interactive lecture covering machine learning basics, language models, and generative AI. No jargon, many analogies.
AI in your classroom: Opportunities and honest limits (40 min): Small group discussion using classroom scenario cards. What would you actually do on Monday?
Resource evaluation framework (30 min): Hands-on practice evaluating three AI literacy resources using a simple rubric. Builds critical judgment for independent curriculum research.
Micro-teach practice (45 min): Each participant selects one concept and teaches a five-minute version to a partner. Partner provides feedback using a structured protocol.
Planning and next steps (20 min): Participants draft a brief integration plan for their own course context.

body.text: Any K–12 educator interested in bringing AI literacy into their teaching, regardless of technical background or subject area. This workshop is not a coding or programming session — it is about concepts, contexts, and classroom practice.

This workshop is designed to be run by a facilitator with strong pedagogical background and working familiarity with AI tools. A facilitator guide with speaker notes, discussion prompts, and common participant questions is available below. Estimated setup time: 30 minutes.
